label.purpose: Paths, IDs, commands and state labels.

shadows.name: transient-surface
shadows.purpose: Task dialog and other transient surfaces.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Use for the single highest-value action in a pane.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 30px; padding: 6px 11px; border: 1px solid #79cfc0; border-radius: 3px; color: #071312; background: #64d2c6; font: 700 11px 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #78e1d4; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #76aef7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Use for supporting actions that remain available without competing with the primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 30px; padding: 6px 11px; border: 1px solid #3a4a5a; border-radius: 3px; color: #b8c5d2; background: #1a232e; font: 400 11px 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #76aef7; color: #e5edf5; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #76aef7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Trace Input
components.description: A compact field for terminal commands, paths and skill sources.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 7px 9px; border: 1px solid #3a4a5a; border-radius: 2px; color: #b8c5d2; background: #121920; font: 400 10px 'SF Mono', monospace; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #76aef7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: A labeled IDE navigation item with a visible active edge and an inline icon.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 31px; padding: 6px 9px; border: 0; border-left: 2px solid transparent; color: #8291a0; background: transparent; font: 400 11px 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; text-align: left; } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-width: 1.5; } .ds-nav-item:hover, .ds-nav-item.is-active { color: #e5edf5; background: #17222c; } .ds-nav-item.is-active { border-left-color: #64d2c6; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #76aef7; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Workbench Pane
components.description: A flat IDE pane that groups task intent, evidence or runtime context.
components.css: .ds-pane { padding: 14px; border: 1px solid #293542; color: #e5edf5; background: #151c25; } .ds-pane h2 { margin: 0 0 7px; font: 600 13px 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; } .ds-pane p { margin: 0; color: #8291a0; font: 400 10px 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
ADE is a focused desktop workbench for software development. Its visual language is deliberately inspired by leading IDEs: the interface is organized around persistent context, dense but readable tools, keyboard-oriented controls and clear state transitions. The work surface should feel operational and calm, with every panel earning its space through a concrete development task.

The system uses dark graphite and navy chrome, cool text, thin structural rules and a restrained cyan accent. It is technical without becoming sterile: success, warning, error and agent states have distinct colors, while depth comes from tonal layering instead of decorative effects.
keyCharacteristics: Familiar IDE grammar: labeled navigation, explorer, command bar, workbench and status bar.
Dense information architecture with short labels and monospace operational metadata.
Flat-by-default surfaces with thin borders and state-driven accents.
No gradients, glassmorphism, marketing hero panels or ornamental imagery.

rules.name: The Signal Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Use cyan, green, amber and red only when they communicate interaction or state; never use them as decoration.

rules.name: The Traceable Type Rule
rules.body: Use the mono face for anything a developer may copy, compare or use to locate evidence; use the sans face for intent and explanation.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: A surface earns elevation only when it is transient or interactive; persistent IDE panes use tonal layering and structural lines.

dos: Do make the current task and its evidence the visual center of the workbench.
Do preserve familiar IDE affordances: tree navigation, command bar, tabs, terminal and status bar.
Do use semantic color for state and keep focus states visible for keyboard users.
Do keep operational labels short and traceable, with paths and IDs in monospace.
donts: Don't turn the workbench into a marketing dashboard of equal-weight metric cards.
Don't use gradients, glassmorphism or decorative illustrations in the desktop shell.
Don't use Unicode glyphs as substitute icons; use inline SVG with an accessible label.
Don't add a rounded container when a structural pane or simple divider communicates the relationship more clearly.
